answers.question: Can I do all three runs next week and add the two I missed?
answers.answer: Short answer: do the three runs, but do not add the two you missed. You are coming off a fever and still coughing, and stacking runs on a tired body is how beginners pick up niggles or get sick again. The race is 8 weeks out, which is plenty of time if you stay consistent week by week. Think of this week as a repeat of the one you missed, not a make-up week.

new.analysis:
## How I read the week

You followed Monday as planned, then illness took Wednesday and Saturday off the table. That is the right call, and the Monday run at 2.78 km was actually your longest to date, so the fitness is still there.

## Why this plan

I am repeating the walk-run shape from the week you missed, not pushing it further. Two short walk-run sessions early, a slightly longer one on Saturday, and real rest days in between. The run bouts stay at 2 minutes with 1 minute walking so your heart and legs settle back into the rhythm you had before the cold.

## What to watch as you run

Keep the running segments conversational, meaning you could speak a short sentence. If the cough worsens during a run, stop and walk home, and give it another day or two. If next week goes smoothly, we will nudge the Saturday session up the week after.

safetyCallouts.title: Return from illness.
safetyCallouts.body: You had a fever as high as 38.4 last week and are still coughing. Keep efforts easy this week, and if the cough gets worse, you feel chest tightness, your heart races at rest, or you feel dizzy on a run, stop and see a GP before running again.
